atoms.text: Aquaponics is a type of farming that combines fish and plant farming into one system. It is a combination of hydroponics, a type of agriculture where the plants do not need soil, and aquaculture, the farming of fish and sea creatures. Aquaponics is a type of indoor farming and most often is done inside greenhouses. It is considered to be more sustainable than other traditional kinds of farming. Fish that work best with aquaponic farming are tilapia, catfish, koi fish and fancy goldfish. Plants that grow the best with aquaponic farming are leafy lettuce, cabbage, kale, carrots, herbs and cauliflower.

Aquaponics is considered a sustainable farming practice for multiple reasons. Firstly, aquaponics needs less water and land and can use the same space to both grow produce and raise fish. Secondly, Food can also be grown year-round because the crops are grown indoors in greenhouses. However, one negative aspect that makes aquaponics less sustainable is that a lot of plastic is required to build the structures.

The symbiotic relationship between the crops and the fish is an extremely important part of aquaponic farming. Plants sit in containers above the fish, and water pumps through the plants and into the water in the fish tank. The plants then clean the water for the fish and return oxygen into the water which the fish need to survive. In turn, the fish provide fertiliser for the soil which has many important nutrients. This is why aquaponics needs less water than traditional farming, because the same water is cycled through the system and used again and again.

text:
A symbiotic relationship is when living things have relationships with one another that benefits at least one of them. Often, but not always, this means that they help one another.

For example, the clownfish and the sea anemone help one another. The sea anemone gives the clownfish shelter, and the clownfish cleans the sea anemone and scares away predator fish.
